title: Curfew In Nepal District After 1 Dead In Communal Violence Near India Border - NDTV
description: Curfew In Nepal District After 1 Dead In Communal Violence Near India Border  NDTV
publisher.title: NDTV
full_article:
An indefinite curfew has been extended in Nepal's Sunsari district near the India border after one person was killed and around 22 others were injured in communal violence earlier this week. Sunsari, situated in southeastern Nepal along the border with India's Bihar, is a crucial transit and commercial corridor between the two countries.

The unrest began during a religious procession, where a disagreement over the use of loud music and religious flags escalated into an altercation between two communities. Police intervened and opened fire to disperse the crowd after the situation spiraled out of control.

One person was killed in the firing, and 22 others, including 13 security force personnel, were injured, police said, according to The Kathmandu Post.

Prime Minister Balendra 'Balen' Shah expressed grief over the violence and appealed for calm. His government has tightened security in parts of the Sunsari district and launched an inquiry into the incident, while also promising compensation for those affected.

Nepali Rupees (NRs) 2,00,000 compensation is promised to the family of the person killed in violence in Sunsari, while the injured people would be provided with NRs 50,000 as treatment expenses, according to Assistant Chief District Officer of Sunsari Poshan Lamichhane.

"The Government of Nepal is committed to providing appropriate compensation to the victims and taking strict legal action against those responsible," the government said in a statement.

The police action has, meanwhile, garnered widespread criticism, with human rights advocates and security experts questioning whether security forces used excessive force. The government has formed a panel to investigate the charges, which is tasked with submitting its report within a week.

The government has also transferred Sunsari chief district officer Basudev Ghimire, Koshi Province Police chief Deputy Inspector General Binod Ghimire, and Sunsari Police chief Keshav Kumar in the face of mounting public pressure over the handling of the violence.

Protesters had demanded action against both the district administration and police leadership.

Key Takeaways:

Dr Tanaka Akihiko visited Nepal July 26–29, his first trip since 2015

Attended Nagdhunga Tunnel inauguration and signed JPY 410m JDS grant

Met ministers to review projects in infrastructure, energy and governance

JICA praised for aviation safety support and decades-long partnership

Japan has reaffirmed its long-term commitment to Nepal's development, with JICA President Dr Tanaka Akihiko concluding a four-day visit focused on infrastructure, human resource development and strengthening bilateral cooperation.

Related Articles Locals protest at Nagdhunga Tunnel opening, Minister promises action on demands Nepal Inaugurates Rs 29 Arba Nagdhunga-Sisnekhola Tunnel

Dr Tanaka visited Nepal from July 26 to 29, marking his first trip since 2015, when he came in the aftermath of the Gorkha earthquake. His latest visit coincided with the 70th anniversary of Nepal–Japan diplomatic relations and comes as Nepal pursues infrastructure expansion and sustainable growth.

During the visit, Dr Tanaka held meetings with Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle, Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, and Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal to review ongoing development projects and discuss future cooperation aligned with Nepal's priorities.

A key highlight was his participation in the Nagdhunga Tunnel inauguration on July 27, Nepal's first road tunnel, expected to improve connectivity between Kathmandu Valley, Pokhara, western Nepal and the Indian border.

Dr Tanaka also attended the signing of a JPY 410 million grant agreement for the Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (JDS), aimed at strengthening Nepal's civil service through higher education and leadership training.

His itinerary included visits to Patan Secondary School, reconstructed with Japanese assistance after the 2015 earthquake, and inspections of JICA-supported aviation safety facilities at Tribhuvan International Airport. The Civil Aviation Authority praised JICA's role in installing radar systems and enhancing aviation personnel capacity.

Reflecting on Nepal's progress, Dr Tanaka said he was encouraged by the country's resilience and reaffirmed JICA's commitment to supporting Nepal's long-term development priorities.

JICA has been one of Nepal's longstanding partners, supporting projects in infrastructure, education, health, disaster resilience and public sector capacity building for decades.

title: Cities need nature: Rethinking public space development in Nepal - The Himalayan Times
description: Cities need nature: Rethinking public space development in Nepal  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
Nepal's cities are expanding rapidly, transforming once-quiet towns into busy urban centres with new roads, buildings, and markets. While this growth has created jobs, improved services, and new opportunities, it has also reduced urban forests, wetlands, farmland, and other natural spaces that keep cities healthy and resilient. This raises an important question: What kind of cities are we building? Urban development should not come at the expense of the ecosystems that sustain life. As climate change intensifies and urban populations grow, protecting urban nature is no longer just an environmental priority, it is essential for public health, climate resilience, and sustainable development.

Sustainable and successful cities are built by balancing social inclusion and environmental stewardship. They invest in resilient infrastructure, protect natural ecosystems, provide accessible public spaces, and ensure that all residents have safe, equitable access to services and opportunities. Cities that integrate nature with development are better prepared to thrive in the face of climate change and rapid urbanization. Parks and open spaces are more than places for recreation, they are living infrastructure that cools cities, manages stormwater, supports biodiversity, and strengthens urban resilience.

Related Articles Department of Passport goes live with new system; public urged to wait out three-month stabilisation period Iran coach says team ordered out of US right after 2-2 draw with New Zealand in World Cup opener

Encouragingly, Nepal is beginning to demonstrate that urban development can follow a different path. Through the Cities 4 Women: Inclusive and Climate Resilient Urbanization in Nepal initiative (Funded by European Union and Government of Finland), seven municipalities are reimagining public open spaces as multifunctional assets that benefit both people and nature. Rather than viewing parks, wetlands, and open areas as undeveloped land awaiting construction, the initiative promotes their protection, restoration, and enhancement as essential urban infrastructure that strengthens biodiversity, climate resilience, livelihoods and community well-being. This represents an important shift in Nepal's approach to urban planning, where public open spaces are increasingly being designed not only for recreation and social inclusion but also for ecological conservation and climate adaptation. Two examples illustrate how this approach is being put into practice.

Let us start with Kamal Pokhari in Tansen. Though modest in size, this urban wetland is alive with fish, amphibians, birds, insects, reptiles, aquatic and semi-aquatic plants. It naturally stores and regulates water, cools the surrounding environment, and serves as an important refuge and stepping-stone habitat for wildlife within an increasingly built-up urban landscape. Yet wetlands like Kamal Pokhari are too often viewed as vacant land waiting for development rather than as vital ecological assets. Through modern planning and nature based design the area is now transferred into a vibrant piece of living infrastructure that serves both people and nature.

Similarly, Hupra Chaur in Hetauda demonstrates how thoughtful urban design can transform open spaces into valuable living infrastructure. The park has been designed to moderate urban heat, improve air quality, store carbon, recharge groundwater, reduce stormwater runoff, and provide habitat for birds, pollinators, and other urban wildlife. Beyond its ecological benefits, it also serves as an emergency evacuation space, supports local livelihoods through a dedicated market area, and offers inclusive spaces

for recreation, environmental education, and community events- strengthening both climate resilience and quality of life.

Biodiversity surveys recorded higher observed species richness and diversity at Hupra Chaur than at Kamal Pokhari. Hupra Chaur had a Shannon Diversity Index of 2.49, compared with 1.83 for Kamal Pokhari. Likewise, the Berger–Parker Dominance Index was higher at Kamal Pokhari (0.36) than at Hupra Chaur (0.26). This suggests that the wetland community was more strongly dominated by a few abundant species. The balanced distribution of species observed at Hupra Chaur is likely attributable to human management practices, including the preferential planting and maintenance of selected species. However, Kamal Pokhari's wetland habitat supports far greater ecological complexity and performs functions that biodiversity indices alone cannot fully capture. Together, these two sites highlight an important lesson: Natural wetlands and well-managed urban green spaces each make unique and complementary contributions to conserving biodiversity, reducing climate risks, and building more resilient cities.

These examples remind us that biodiversity is not something that exists only in national parks or protected forests. It also belongs in our cities. Unfortunately, many urban landscaping projects still favour ornamental exotic plants chosen mainly for their appearance. While attractive, many provide little value for local wildlife, and some even become invasive, displacing native species. Planting indigenous trees, shrubs, and flowering plants would create habitats for birds, butterflies, and bees while requiring less maintenance because they are naturally adapted to local conditions.

This calls for a different way to look into the planning of our cities. Biodiversity should not be treated as an afterthought but as essential urban infrastructure. Municipalities should protect mature trees, restore wetlands instead of filling them, create green corridors along rivers and roads, increase permeable surfaces, and make ecological mapping a standard part of urban planning. Even relatively small design decisions can significantly improve the ecological value of urban spaces and substantially increase habitat quality and ecological connectivity. These include retaining deadwood where safe, planting native vegetation, creating nesting opportunities for birds and bats, nest boxes, providing water sources for wildlife, reducing unnecessary night lighting, creating wildlife passages, ecological corridors, amphibian tunnels beneath roads, pollinator-friendly planting, and nature-inclusive infrastructure into new developments and urban renewal projects. These measures recognise that even highly urbanised landscapes can support biodiversity when cities are intentionally designed to accommodate the needs of wildlife.

These are not environmental luxuries. They are practical investments in safer, healthier, and more resilient cities. Healthy ecosystems reduce flood risks, improve air quality, moderate urban temperatures, lower heat-related health costs, store carbon, support pollinators, enhance mental well-being, and make cities more attractive places to live and invest. We also need to rethink how we measure progress. Instead of celebrating only the kilometres of roads paved or buildings constructed, we should also ask: How many wetlands were protected? How many mature and native trees were conserved? How many hectares of connected habitat were restored? Are more birds, butterflies, and pollinators returning? Are our cities becoming cooler, healthier, and more resilient? These are equally meaningful indicators of sustainable urban development.

As Nepal continues to urbanize, we face a simple choice. We can continue replacing nature with concrete and pay the environmental price later. Or we can design cities where development and nature work together. The experience from municipalities across Nepal shows that this is not only possible - it is already happening. Parks, wetlands, river corridors, and community open spaces can become climate refuges, biodiversity havens, and healthier places for everyone. The debate is no longer about whether Nepal should invest in nature-based urban planning. It is about whether we are willing to leave future generations to bear the cost of our inaction.

सामाजिक समावेश आ पर्यावरण संचालन कें संतुलन बना क टिकाऊ आ सफल शहरक कें निर्माण कैल जायत छै. ओ लचीला बुनियादी ढाँचा मे निवेश करयत छै, प्राकृतिक पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र कें सुरक्षा करयत छै, सुलभ सार्वजनिक स्थान प्रदान करयत छै, आ इ सुनिश्चित करयत छै की सब निवासीक कें सेवाक आ अवसरक कें सुरक्षित, समान रूप सं पहुंच छै. जे शहर प्रकृति कें विकास कें साथ एकीकृत करय छै, जलवायु परिवर्तन आ तेजी सं शहरीकरण कें सामना करय कें लेल बेहतर ढंग सं तैयार छै. पार्क आ खुला जगह मनोरंजन कें लेल जगह सं बेसि छै, इ जीवित बुनियादी ढाँचा छै जे शहरक कें ठंडा करय छै, आंधी-तूफान कें पानी कें प्रबंधन करय छै, जैव विविधता कें समर्थन करय छै, आ शहरी लचीलापन कें मजबूत करय छै.

संबंधित लेख पासपोर्ट विभाग नव प्रणाली के संग लाइव भ गेल; जनता स॑ तीन महीना के स्थिरीकरण अवधि के इंतजार करै के आग्रह ईरान केरऽ कोच न॑ कहलकै कि विश्व कप केरऽ ओपनर मैच म॑ न्यूजीलैंड के साथ २-२ स॑ बराबरी के ठीक बाद टीम न॑ अमेरिका स॑ बाहर निकलै के आदेश देलकै

उत्साहवर्धक बात ई जे नेपाल ई देखाबय लागल अछि जे शहरी विकास एकटा अलग बाट पर चलि सकैत अछि । शहर 4 महिला: नेपाल मे समावेशी आ जलवायु लचीला शहरीकरण पहल (यूरोपीय संघ आ फिनलैंड सरकार कें वित्त पोषित) कें माध्यम सं सात नगरपालिका सार्वजनिक खुला स्थानक कें बहुकार्यात्मक संपत्ति कें रूप मे पुनर्कल्पना कयर रहल छै जे लोग आ प्रकृति दूनू कें लाभ पहुंचाबय छै. पार्क, आर्द्रभूमि आ खुला क्षेत्रक कें निर्माण कें इंतजार मे अविकसित जमीन कें रूप मे देखय कें बजाय, इ पहल ओकर सुरक्षा, बहाली आ संवर्धन कें आवश्यक शहरी बुनियादी ढाँचा कें रूप मे बढ़ावा देयत छै जे जैव विविधता, जलवायु लचीलापन, आजीविका आ सामुदायिक कल्याण कें मजबूत करयत छै. ई शहरी नियोजन के प्रति नेपाल के दृष्टिकोण में एकटा महत्वपूर्ण बदलाव के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै, जहां सार्वजनिक खुला स्थान के डिजाइन न सिर्फ मनोरंजन आरू सामाजिक समावेश के लेलऽ बल्कि पारिस्थितिकी संरक्षण आरू जलवायु अनुकूलन के लेलऽ भी तेजी स॑ करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । दूटा उदाहरण इ दर्शाबैत अछि जे एहि दृष्टिकोण कए कोना व्यवहार मे उतारल जा रहल अछि।

शुरुआत करी तानसेन मे कमल पोखरी स। आकार में मामूली होय के बावजूद ई शहरी आर्द्रभूमि माछ, उभयचर, पक्षी, कीड़ा-मकोड़ा, सरीसृप, जलीय आरू अर्ध-जलीय पौधा के साथ जीवित छै । ई प्राकृतिक रूप स॑ पानी के संग्रहण आरू नियंत्रण करै छै, आसपास के वातावरण क॑ ठंडा करै छै, आरू बढ़त॑ जाय रहलऽ शहरी परिदृश्य के भीतर वन्यजीवऽ लेली एगो महत्वपूर्ण शरण आरू सीढ़ी वाला आवास के रूप म॑ काम करै छै । तइयो कमल पोखरी जैसनऽ आर्द्रभूमि क॑ बहुत बार महत्वपूर्ण पारिस्थितिकी संपत्ति के रूप म॑ नै बल्कि विकास के इंतजार म॑ खाली जमीन के रूप म॑ देखलऽ जाय छै । आधुनिक योजना आरू प्रकृति आधारित डिजाइन के माध्यम स॑ ई क्षेत्र क॑ अब॑ जीवित बुनियादी ढाँचा केरऽ एगो जीवंत टुकड़ा म॑ स्थानांतरित करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै जे लोगऽ आरू प्रकृति दूनू के सेवा करै छै ।

तहिना हेटौड़ा के हुपरा चौर ई दर्शाबैत अछि जे कोना सोचल-समझल शहरी डिजाइन खुला स्थान के मूल्यवान रहय के बुनियादी ढांचा मे बदलि सकैत अछि । ई पार्क क॑ शहरी गर्मी क॑ मध्यम करै, हवा के गुणवत्ता म॑ सुधार, कार्बन के संग्रहण, भूजल क॑ रिचार्ज करै, आंधी पानी के बहाव क॑ कम करै, आरू पक्षी, परागणक आरू अन्य शहरी वन्यजीवऽ लेली आवास उपलब्ध करै लेली डिजाइन करलऽ गेलऽ छै । अपन पारिस्थितिकी लाभ सं परे, इ आपातकालीन निकासी कें स्थान कें रूप मे सेहो काज करयत छै, एकटा समर्पित बाजार क्षेत्र कें माध्यम सं स्थानीय आजीविका कें समर्थन करयत छै, आ समावेशी स्थान प्रदान करयत छै

मनोरंजन, पर्यावरण शिक्षा, आ सामुदायिक आयोजनक कें लेल- जलवायु लचीलापन आ जीवन कें गुणवत्ता दूनू कें मजबूत करनाय.

जैव विविधता सर्वेक्षण म॑ कमल पोखरी के तुलना म॑ हुपरा चौर म॑ अधिक देखलऽ गेलऽ प्रजाति समृद्धि आरू विविधता दर्ज करलऽ गेलऽ छै । हुपरा चौर के शैनन विविधता सूचकांक 2.49 रहल, जखन कि कमल पोखरी के 1.83 रहल। तहिना बर्गर-पार्कर डोमिनेंस इंडेक्स हुपरा चौर (0.26) के अपेक्षा कमल पोखरी (0.36) मे बेसी रहल। एहि सँ ई बुझना जाइत अछि जे आर्द्रभूमि समुदाय मे किछु प्रचुर प्रजातिक बेसी मजबूती छल । हुपरा चौर म॑ देखलऽ गेलऽ प्रजाति केरऽ संतुलित वितरण के कारण संभवतः मानव प्रबंधन प्रथा छै, जेकरा म॑ चयनित प्रजाति केरऽ तरजीही रोपनी आरू रखरखाव शामिल छै । लेकिन कमल पोखरी केरऽ आर्द्रभूमि केरऽ आवास कहीं अधिक पारिस्थितिकी जटिलता के समर्थन करै छै आरू ऐन्हऽ कार्य करै छै जेकरा केवल जैव विविधता सूचकांक पूरा तरह स॑ कैप्चर नै करी सकै छै । इ दूनू स्थल मिल क एकटा महत्वपूर्ण पाठ कें उजागर करयत छै: प्राकृतिक आर्द्रभूमि आ सुप्रबंधित शहरी हरियर स्थान प्रत्येक जैव विविधता कें संरक्षण, जलवायु जोखिम कें कम करय आ बेसि लचीला शहरक कें निर्माण मे अद्वितीय आ पूरक योगदान देयत छै.

ई उदाहरण हमरा सब क॑ याद दिलाबै छै कि जैव विविधता ऐन्हऽ चीज नै छै जे केवल राष्ट्रीय उद्यान या संरक्षित जंगलऽ म॑ ही मौजूद छै । ई हमरा सभक शहरक सेहो अछि। दुर्भाग्यवश, बहुत सारा शहरी लैंडस्केपिंग परियोजना अखनी भी सजावटी विदेशी पौधा के पक्षधर छै जेकरा मुख्य रूप स॑ ओकरऽ रूप लेली चुनलऽ जाय छै । आकर्षक होय के साथ-साथ बहुत सारा स्थानीय वन्यजीव केरऽ मूल्य कम दै छै, आरू कुछ त॑ आक्रामक भी होय जाय छै, जेकरा स॑ देशी प्रजाति केरऽ विस्थापित होय जाय छै । देशी गाछ, झाड़ी आ फूल वाला पौधाक कें रोपनी सं चिड़ै, तितली आ मधुमक्खी कें लेल आवास बनतय जखन कि रखरखाव कें आवश्यकता कम होयत, कियाकि इ प्राकृतिक रूप सं स्थानीय परिस्थितिक कें अनुकूल होयत छै.

एहि लेल अपन शहर क योजना कए देखबाक एकटा अलग तरीका स जरूरत अछि। जैव विविधता कें एकटा आफ्टर थॉट कें रूप मे नहि बल्कि आवश्यक शहरी बुनियादी ढाँचा कें रूप मे देखल जेबाक चाही. नगरपालिकाक कें परिपक्व गाछक कें सुरक्षा करनाय चाही, आर्द्रभूमिक कें भरय कें बजाय ओकरा बहाल करनाय चाही, नदी आ सड़कक कें किनारे हरियर गलियारा बनानाय चाही, पारगम्य सतहक कें बढ़ावा देनाय चाही, आ पारिस्थितिकी मानचित्रण कें शहरी योजना कें मानक हिस्सा बनानाय चाही. अपेक्षाकृत छोट डिजाइन निर्णयक सं सेहो शहरी स्थानक कें पारिस्थितिक मूल्य मे काफी सुधार भ सकय छै आ आवास कें गुणवत्ता आ पारिस्थितिकी संपर्क मे काफी वृद्धि भ सकय छै. एहि मे मृत लकड़ी कें सुरक्षित स्थान पर रखनाय, देशी वनस्पति कें रोपनी, पक्षी आ चमगादड़क कें लेल घोंसला बनावा कें अवसर पैदा करनाय, घोंसला कें डिब्बा, वन्यजीवक कें लेल जल स्रोत उपलब्ध करानाय, रात कें अनावश्यक रोशनी कें कम करनाय, वन्यजीव मार्ग, पारिस्थितिकी गलियारा, सड़कक कें नीचा उभयचर सुरंग बनानाय, परागणक कें अनुकूल रोपनी, आ प्रकृति-समावेशी बुनियादी ढाँचा कें नव मे शामिल करनाय शामिल छै विकास आ शहरी नवीकरण परियोजना। इ उपायक इ बात कें मान्यता देयत छै की अत्यधिक शहरी परिदृश्य सेहो जैव विविधता कें समर्थन कयर सकय छै जखन शहरक कें जानबूझ क वन्यजीवक कें जरूरतक कें पूरा करय कें लेल डिजाइन कैल गेल छै.

ई सभ पर्यावरणक विलासिता नहि थिक। इ सुरक्षित, स्वस्थ आ बेसि लचीला शहरक मे व्यावहारिक निवेश छै. स्वस्थ पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र बाढ़ कें जोखिम कें कम करएयत छै, हवा कें गुणवत्ता मे सुधार करएयत छै, शहरी तापमान मे सुधार करएयत छै, गर्मी सं संबंधित स्वास्थ्य लागत कें कम करएयत छै, कार्बन कें संग्रहण करएयत छै, परागणक कें समर्थन करएयत छै, मानसिक कल्याण कें बढ़ावा देयत छै, आ शहरक कें रहनाय आ निवेश कें लेल बेसि आकर्षक जगह बनायत छै. हमरा सब कए एहि पर सेहो फेर स विचार करबाक जरूरत अछि जे हम सब प्रगति कए कोना नापब। केवल पक्का सड़क या निर्माण के किलोमीटर के उत्सव मनाबय के बजाय हमरा सब के इहो पूछय के चाही जे कतेक आर्द्रभूमि के संरक्षण भेल? कतेक परिपक्व आ देशी गाछक संरक्षण भेल? कतेक हेक्टेयर जुडल आवास बहाली भेल? की बेसी चिड़ै, तितली आ परागणकर्त्ता वापस आबि रहल अछि? की हमर शहर ठंडा, स्वस्थ आ लचीला भ रहल अछि? इ सब सतत शहरी विकास कें ओतबे सार्थक सूचक छै.

जेना-जेना नेपाल शहरीकरण होइत रहल अछि, हमरा लोकनि केँ एकटा सरल विकल्पक सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि। प्रकृति के जगह कंक्रीट लगाबैत रहि सकैत छी आ बाद मे पर्यावरणीय दाम चुका सकैत छी। या फेर एहन शहर के डिजाइन क सकय छी जतय विकास आ प्रकृति मिल क काज करय. नेपाल भरिक नगरपालिकासभक अनुभवसँ पता चलैत अछि जे ई मात्र संभव नहि - पहिनेसँ भऽ रहल अछि । पार्क, आर्द्रभूमि, नदी गलियारा, आ सामुदायिक खुला स्थान जलवायु शरण, जैव विविधता कें ठिकाना, आ सब कें लेल स्वस्थ जगह बइन सकय छै. आब एहि पर बहस नहि अछि जे नेपाल कए प्रकृति आधारित शहरी नियोजन मे निवेश करबाक चाही। ई बात छै कि की हम्मं॑ अपनऽ निष्क्रियता के कीमत उठाबै लेली आबै वाला पीढ़ी क॑ छोड़ी क॑ जाय लेली तैयार छियै कि नै ।

Lal Bahadur Rai, a resident of Tekunala in Dhankuta Municipality-8, died on July 26 while undergoing treatment after falling seriously ill during duty at a company in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, according to his family.

Kathmandu, July 30: A Chinese climber, who successfully scaled both Mt Sagarmatha and Lhotse in the spring season of 2026, has been honoured.

The Chinese climber, Shi Jungi, as well as Nepali guides—Nigma Tamang and Dawa Nuru Sherpa, had scaled Mt Sagarmath on May 14, 2026 and Mt Lhotse on May 18 through Himalayan Mountaineering Expedition were honoured.

Coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party and former Prime Minister, Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda' today honoured them for non-stop expediting two mountains in a single season.

Though most of climbers scale Mt Lhotse descending to camp-IIII after successful expedition of Mt Sagarmatha, the team of Shi Jungi, had scaled the Mt Lhotse descending to camp-II.

On the occasion, Coordinator Dahal highly praised the indomitable courage and progressive spirit of the team.

"The continuous expedition of Mt Sagarmatha and Lhotse in a single season examine the physical stamina, technical skill and mental fortitude of climbers. The team has further expanded the boundaries of global mountaineering," he underlined.

Coordinator Dahal spoke of his emotional connection with mountains. Recalling that his late son Prakash Dahal had also climbed Mt Sagarmatha, he argued that he has deep respect for every mountaineer who respected mountains and undergo safely expedition.

He also expressed the belief that the people-level mountaineering relations between China and Nepal would further strengthen cultural relations of both countries.

Similarly, the Chinese expeditor shared that he got full support from Nepali guides in his historical achievement.

He assured of actively involving to take mountaineering and Nepal-China relations to a new height in coming days.(RSS)

काठमांडू, ३० जुलाई : २०२६ केरऽ वसंत ऋतु म॑ माउंट सागरमाथा आरू ल्होत्से दोनों जगह सफलतापूर्वक स्केल करै वाला चीनी पर्वतारोही क॑ सम्मानित करलऽ गेलै ।

चीनी पर्वतारोही शी जंगी के साथ-साथ नेपाली गाइड-निग्मा तामांग आरू दावा नूरू शेर्पा, 14 मई, 2026 क॑ माउंट सागरमाथ आरू 18 मई क॑ माउंट ल्होत्से क॑ हिमालयन पर्वतारोहण अभियान के माध्यम स॑ स्केल करी क॑ सम्मानित करलऽ गेलै ।

नेपाली कम्युनिस्ट पार्टीके संयोजक आ पूर्व प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल ‘प्रचण्ड’ आइ एकहि मौसममे दू टा पहाड़के नॉन स्टॉप गति प्रदान करबाक लेल सम्मानित कएलनि ।

यद्यपि अधिकांश पर्वतारोही माउंट सागरमाथाक सफल अभियानक पछाति कैम्प-IIII पर उतरैत माउंट ल्होत्से स्केल करैत छथि, शि जुंगीक टीम, कैम्प-II पर उतरैत माउंट ल्होत्से पर चढ़ि गेल छल.

एहि अवसर पर संयोजक दाहाल टीमक अदम्य साहस आ प्रगतिशील भावनाक बेस प्रशंसा केलनि ।

हुनी रेखांकित करलकै, "एक सीजन मँ माउंट सागरमाथा आरू ल्होत्से केरौ लगातार अभियान पर्वतारोही सिनी के शारीरिक सहनशक्ति, तकनीकी कौशल आरू मानसिक धैर्य के जांच करै छै । टीम नँ वैश्विक पर्वतारोहण के सीमा क आरू विस्तारित करलकै ।

संयोजक दाहाल पहाड़ स अपन भावनात्मक संबंध क गप केलथि। हुनकऽ स्वर्गीय पुत्र प्रकाश दाहाल भी माउंट सागरमाथा पर चढ़ी गेलऽ छेलै, ई बात क॑ याद करतें हुअ॑ हुनकऽ तर्क छेलै कि पहाड़ केरऽ सम्मान करै वाला आरू सुरक्षित अभियान स॑ गुजरै वाला हर पर्वतारोही के प्रति हुनका गहरा सम्मान छै ।

चीन आ नेपाल के बीच जनस्तरीय पर्वतारोहण संबंध स दुनु देश के सांस्कृतिक संबंध आओर मजबूत होयत से विश्वास सेहो व्यक्त केलनि।

तहिना चीनी अभियानी साझा केलथि जे हुनका अपन ऐतिहासिक उपलब्धि मे नेपाली गाइड स पूर्ण सहयोग भेटल ।

आगामी दिन मे पर्वतारोहण आ नेपाल-चीन संबंध कए नव ऊंचाई पर ल जेबा लेल सक्रिय रूप स संलग्न हेबाक आश्वासन देलथि।(आरएसएस)
